title: Internal and sectionwise module operations agree
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For each scheme $T$ use the small pro-étale site with its universe convention [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the sheafified tensor product of abelian sheaves [det-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor-structure], the pulled-back ring object $\Lambda_T$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and its reconstructed section-ring sheaf $B_T$. Let
$$E_T:\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T}(\operatorname{Sh}(T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\mathrm{Ab}))\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(B_T)$$
be the canonical equivalence of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Write $f^*_{\rm int},f_{*,\rm int}$ for the internal module functors and their specified adjunction [def-sfb-module-upper-star], [def-sfb-module-lower-star], [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction]. For $f:T'\to T$ let $f^*_{\rm sec},f_{*,\rm sec}$ be the sectionwise ringed-topos functors for the ring isomorphism $f^{-1}B_T\cong B_{T'}$ induced by $\alpha_f$ [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]: pullback is $B_{T'}\otimes_{f^{-1}B_T}f^{-1}(-)$ (sheafified sectionwise tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]), and direct image is ordinary sheaf direct image with scalar restriction along the adjunct $B_T\to f_*B_{T'}$, with their canonical adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]. Then the canonical comparisons give
$$E_{T'}f^*_{\rm int}\cong f^*_{\rm sec}E_T,\qquad E_Tf_{*,\rm int}\cong f_{*,\rm sec}E_{T'},$$
and identify the specified internal adjunction with the sectionwise ringed-topos adjunction, including its unit and counit. For an open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow T$, write $j_{!,\rm int}$ for [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] and $j_{!,\rm sec}$ for the sectionwise extension by zero, the left adjoint to $j^*_{\rm sec}$. There is a canonical comparison
$$E_Tj_{!,\rm int}\cong j_{!,\rm sec}E_U$$
identifying these open adjunctions. In a cartesian square of schemes with open vertical immersions and compatible pulled-back coefficients, these comparisons identify the internal open-extension base-change transformation with the sectionwise one (the transformation defined as the adjunction mate of the pullback-composition comparison). Thus whenever that sectionwise transformation is invertible, so is the internal one. The equivalences $E_T$ are additive exact equivalences, so exactness and exact sequences of these operations transport between the two module categories.

proof.text: The equivalences $E_T$ leave sheaves and maps unchanged, hence preserve sums of morphisms. Their quasi-inverses are additive too: apply the faithful additive $E_T$ to an asserted sum identity and use the natural counit to identify its two sides.

source.place: Canonical lax tensor maps of continuous pro-étale direct image; component evaluation made explicit in WeilConjectures/CategoryTheory/Sites/PushforwardMonoidal.lean, lines 94–123.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-pushforward-comp-monoidal] (for the symmetric coefficients $\mathrm{Ab}$ its maps are the lax structure $\mu$ used in [def-sfb-module-lower-star]), $\mu_{F,G}(V)\circ q_{f_*F,f_*G,V}=q_{F,G,V'}$, where $q$ is the tensor-sheafification unit on sections and $V'=V\times_TT'$. With naturality of $q$ in its first argument, the action composite of [def-sfb-module-lower-star] sends $q(r\otimes n)$, $r\in\Lambda_T(V)$, $n\in N(V')$, to $a_{V'}q(\eta_f(r)\otimes n)$. The section action reconstructed by $E_T$ is therefore $(r,n)\mapsto\eta_f(r)n$. Since $\eta_f=f_*\alpha_f\circ\eta_f^{\rm Ab}$ is the prescribed coefficient adjunct, the identity sheaf map is the natural linear comparison $r_f:E_Tf_{*,\rm int}\cong f_{*,\rm sec}E_{T'}$.

source.place: Characterization of the canonical lax tensor map of a pro-étale pushforward by its composite with the sheafification maps; the pure-tensor action evaluation is agent-written.

proof.text: For the specified internal and ringed-topos adjunctions take $c_f^{-1}$ to be the inverse mate of $r_f$. The inverse-mate lemma makes it invertible. The transpose lemma identifies their full Hom bijections; evaluating these bijections on identities identifies their units and counits. Mate bijectivity fixes this comparison uniquely.

proof.text: Apply the same inverse-mate and transpose lemmas to $j_{!,\rm int}\dashv j^*_{\rm int}$, the specified sectionwise open adjunction, and right comparison $c_j$. This gives $o_j:E_Tj_{!,\rm int}\cong j_{!,\rm sec}E_U$, identifying the Hom bijections and therefore both units and counits.

proof.text: The direct-image compositor and $r_f,r_g,r_{gf}$ are identity maps on the same rebracketed sections, so their composition square commutes. Apply the adjunction-evaluation composition lemma with evaluation functors $E_T$, right squares $r$, and left comparisons $c$ of Step 3. It identifies the pullback compositors, which are the specified conjugates of these direct-image compositors.

proof.text:
In the open square write $b:g'^*j^*\cong j'^*g^*$. Its left mate is
$$\beta=\varepsilon_{j'}g^*j_!\circ j'_!(b j_!)\circ j'_!g'^*(\eta_j).$$
Step 5 identifies $b$ and Step 4 identifies the two adjunction factors. Mate pasting therefore identifies this composite with the sectionwise mate. Conjugation by the comparison isomorphisms and reflection by $E_{T'}$ transfer its invertibility.

proof.text: Closed sheaf tensor preserves colimits, so internal modules are abelian; sectionwise modules are abelian by the site-size convention. Apply the additive-equivalence lemma to $E_T$ and its additive inverse: both preserve exact sequences. Their unit/counit isomorphisms then reflect exactness. Substituting the functor comparisons above transports exactness of every operation.
